--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[PAY-1] Server trusts client-side amounts when creating payments
File: src/app/api/checkout/razorpay-order/route.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: The API creates a Razorpay order using amount taken directly from the client body and returns that order to the client; the checkout page also computes and sends the amount from the browser to /api/checkout/razorpay-order and /api/checkout/verify-payment rather than the server deriving it from the DB order. verify-payment also never validates the paid amount against the server order total. This lets a malicious client create/pay a much smaller amount and get the DB order confirmed.
Impact: Underpaid or manipulated orders will be accepted and stock decremented, causing direct revenue loss and fulfillment of unpaid goods under production traffic.
Fix: Always read the authoritative total from the server-side order (DB) and use that when creating Razorpay orders and when verifying payments; reject mismatched amounts and/or requery Razorpay for payment details server-side.

[PAY-2] Webhook processing is non-idempotent and can duplicate shipments
File: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The webhook verifies the signature but never records the webhook event id or checks for prior processing; on payment captured it unconditionally creates a Shiprocket order and updates DB fields without de-duplication checks. Duplicate webhook deliveries or retries will re-run Shiprocket creation.
Impact: Duplicate Shiprocket orders / duplicate fulfillment and shipping costs (and potential customer confusion) leading to real financial loss and reconciliation headaches under retries/high traffic.
Fix: Persist incoming webhook event IDs (unique constraint) and short-circuit already-processed events; make Shiprocket creation idempotent (skip if shiprocketOrderId already set) or implement an at-least-once-safe retry/de-duplication strategy.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[PAY-3] Coupon quantity is decremented outside an atomic purchase transaction
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L320)
Evidence: When a coupon with limited quantity is used, the code updates/decrements coupon.quantity before creating the order and not inside a single DB transaction with order creation.
Impact: If order creation fails after decrement, coupon uses are lost (or if concurrency races occur, quantity can be overspent), causing incorrect coupon accounting and potential revenue leakage or customer disputes.
Fix: Wrap coupon reservation/decrement and order creation in a single transaction or implement a reservation/rollback mechanism for coupon usage.

[PAY-4] Payment ↔ DB reconciliation race: webhook vs client verification
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: verify-payment (client-driven) marks order CONFIRMED and stores razorpayPaymentId, while the webhook also updates order status and triggers fulfilment flows but does not set the payment IDs or guard against races; neither side validates amounts against the authoritative order.
Impact: Race conditions can produce orders with missing payment IDs or inconsistent state, causing failed reconciliation, duplicate or missed fulfillments, and accounting errors as traffic scales.
Fix: Make server-side finalization authoritative (validate payments using webhook or by calling Razorpay API), have webhook set payment IDs and be idempotent, and avoid relying solely on client-driven verify calls.

--- INFO ---

[PAY-5] Razorpay + webhook signature verification present
File: package.json / src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts
Evidence: repository includes the razorpay package and the webhook handler verifies x-razorpay-signature via HMAC using RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
